| `WJ-094` | Server-side cron for scheduled runs | ✅ Done | `GET /api/cron/scheduled-runs` (Vercel Cron, `vercel.json`; `CRON_SECRET` bearer, 503 without one) fires every tenant's due schedules with nobody's tab open. `server/workflow/dueTenants.ts` asks the database which tenants have work (`wonderjobs.due_schedule_tenants`, migration `0004`) instead of pulling every workflow document; `server/workflow/snapshot.ts` loads a tenant's career/jobs/workflow/automation documents in the client's own persisted shape (`server/clientState.ts`) and writes them back with the same trimming the browser's `partialize` applies; `server/workflow/serverExecutors.ts` runs profile → search → dedupe → understand → match → quality → rank through the **same** `WorkflowEngine` the browser uses, against `server/jobs/search.ts`. Stages needing the candidate (prepare, review, apply) are deliberately not run — the shortlist, saved jobs and a notification are waiting when they next sign in. Idempotent by construction: the schedule's `nextRunAt` advances *before* the run starts, so a crash or a timeout can never re-fire in a loop; one run per tenant per tick, skipped while another run is active; per-tenant 60 s and per-invocation 240 s budgets. Schedule times are now evaluated in the schedule's own timezone (`domain/workflow/schedule.ts`, DST-aware, 8 unit tests) — the old `setHours` version would have moved everyone's 08:00 to 08:00 UTC once the cron owned it; the browser uses the same function. Cadence is a deployment fact, not an assumption: Vercel's Hobby plan runs a cron **once a day** (a `*/15` schedule fails the build there), which is a safety net rather than a scheduler, so `vercel.json` ships `0 2 * * *` and the browser keeps firing schedules at their proper time. `CRON_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (default 1440) declares the real cadence; at or below 60 the cron owns scheduling and the client ticker stands down (`server/workflow/cronCadence.ts`, reported to the browser by `/api/jobs/sources`). They can never double-fire either way: one `isDue` rule — shared by the browser, the cron and the SQL — skips a schedule that already ran in the last 12 hours, which is shorter than the gap between any two legitimate firings this product can express. 7 unit tests cover firing, publishing the catalog, notifying, staying silent when the condition isn't met, advancing on failure, skipping review-only schedules and refusing to start a second concurrent run. |
| `WJ-097` | Follow-up and interview reminders from the server | ✅ Done | The cron's second pass (`server/workflow/reminders.ts`, same `/api/cron/scheduled-runs` invocation) raises the reminders the browser's ticker used to raise only while a tab was open — an interview on Tuesday is exactly what someone needs told to them on Monday. Tenants with something near enough to matter come from `wonderjobs.due_reminder_tenants` (migration `0006`, a jsonb query over applications' follow-ups) instead of reading every tenant's applications. Lead times match the browser's: two days for an interview, one for a follow-up, and still worth saying for a day after it was due. Idempotent through the **same** `career.reminded` list the browser writes, so the two can never raise the same reminder twice, and the career document is merged rather than replaced so a concurrent tab doesn't lose work. Each reminder is also pushed (WJ-096). Reminders run even when the schedule pass has eaten most of the invocation's budget: a missed interview reminder is worse than a late run. 10 unit tests. |

Affected jobs get a `highlights` chip (“Similar to roles you've marked not for me”). `LearnedPreferences` on the Career DNA page lists every active signal with its evidence and lets the candidate confirm or **Turn off** one (dismissal is remembered and never resurfaces — spec §18: “provide a way to review learned preferences”). Nothing here writes to Career DNA itself; only ranking is affected, matching the spec's distinction between an automatic ranking adaptation and a confirmed preference change. 21 tests (`domain/career/learning.test.ts` ×17, `services/jobs/matching.learning.test.ts` ×4). Full fixture results in `docs/LEARNING_EVALUATION_REPORT.md`. **Known gap:** `wrong_location`/`compensation`/`skills_mismatch`/`not_interested`/`other` reasons are recorded but don't yet drive a ranking rule; positive-evidence learning (saves/applications → suggest a preference increase, per spec §35's own worked example) is not implemented — this pass covered only the literal false “not for me” claim. |

Every catalog job hidden by an active filter (saved-only, work mode, source, minimum fit, freshness, minimum salary, search text) or by “not for me” is attributed to the *first* reason it fails, in the same order the filters actually apply, so counts never double up past the total (asserted directly: hidden-reason counts + visible count == total catalog). `FilteredBreakdown` shows a compact “Showing N of M — K hidden: …” line above results when some are hidden, or a full explanation with the spec's required **Show me anyway / Change my preferences** actions when every result is hidden — replacing a generic “No jobs match these filters” with an honest breakdown by reason, never blank. “Show me anyway” and the filter bar's own “Clear filters” now share one `CLEAR_FILTERS_PATCH` constant so they can't drift apart. | `WJ-111` | "Is this a fake run?" — Run Wonder searched a canned "product manager", not the candidate's role | ✅ Done | A signed-in candidate whose goal was "iam senior director" got "110 jobs read, none scored above 70" twice and reasonably asked whether anything real was happening. Verified end to end before answering: signed-in runs use `RemoteSourceAdapter` → `/api/jobs/search` → the live public APIs in `server/jobs/providers.ts` (mock universe is gated to demo/local via `getClientMode().mode !== "user"`, and `store/jobs.ts` never seeds a real account); Vercel production runtime logs show the run's outbound fetches to Ashby/Greenhouse/Lever boards, Jobicy, Remote OK and Himalayas; and reproducing the search from this sandbox returned 111 real postings for "product manager" in Bengaluru (Stripe, Airbnb, ClickUp, DomainTools…) — the same 110 came back twice because the server caches a query for 10–15 minutes. So the data was real, but the *search* was not the candidate's: `runs/new` initialised the query to a hardcoded `"product manager"` and fell back to it when blank, hidden inside the collapsed "Search details". A senior director was shown 110 product-manager jobs and, correctly, 0 matches. Fixed at the root: `defaultSearchQuery(dna)` (`services/jobs/normalize.ts`) derives the query from the candidate's own headline ("Product Manager · Consumer & Fintech" → "product manager"), else their goal with a leading "I am / I'm / iam" stripped ("iam senior director" → "senior director" — left in, "iam" reads as identity-and-access-management and returns 4 IAM engineering jobs), dropping industry words (scored separately by Career DNA) and keeping seniority; when nothing can be derived it returns "" and the setup page opens Search details, marks the field required and keeps Continue disabled with "Add a search query" — it never substitutes a role. The run page now states its provenance under the status line: "Searched “…” in … across N live sources · change the search". Added a **Real data only** section to `CLAUDE.md` (signed-in accounts see only fetched/computed data; never substitute a default for intent; say "needs setup"/"unavailable" instead of filling gaps; show provenance; verify against code and production logs before claiming). 4 unit tests. `npm run check` 206/206; golden journeys 10/10. |
| `WJ-114` | A run on the user's own imported CV failed with "No jobs matched your search" — for any query | ✅ Done | Followed directly from WJ-113: with the CV importing correctly, the next run still failed. Reproduced with real `searchSource()` calls against the live boards (not a guess): the auto-derived query `"target senior director svp"` returned 0 results on all 4 sources; `"senior director svp"` (drop "target") returned 1; `"director"` alone returned 155 — the query itself was the problem, and two separate causes stacked. (1) `defaultSearchQuery` read the candidate's headline verbatim, but this headline literally starts `"Target: Senior Director / SVP — …"` — a meta-label the candidate wrote to mean "my target role is…", not part of the title. Sent literally, `titleMatches` required the literal word "target" in every posting's title, which no real job ever has. New `stripHeadlineLabel()` drops a leading `target:`/`goal:`/`seeking:`/`objective:`/`desired role:`/`looking for:`/`open to:`/`career goal:` label (any separator: `:`, `-`, `–`, `—`) before the headline is read, mirroring how `stripSelfReference` already handles a goal starting "I am…". (2) Even past that, `"svp"` wasn't in `SENIORITY_WORDS`, so `corePhrase` treated it as a required *role* word rather than a seniority qualifier (unlike its synonym `"vp"`, which already was) — requiring the literal substring "svp" in a posting's title on top of "iam" is far narrower than the search actually needs. Added `svp`, `evp` and `chief` alongside the existing level words. Re-ran the exact reported search live end to end after both fixes: `"senior director svp iam"` → `corePhrase` resolves to just `"iam"` → 3 real postings back (Coinbase, Canonical, Vercel — a genuinely niche Mumbai-based senior IAM search on free public job-board APIs; small but real and no longer a hard failure). Also verified in a real browser: setting Career DNA's headline to the exact reported string and opening Run Wonder now shows `"senior director svp iam"` in the search summary, not `"target senior director svp"`. 5 new unit tests. `npm run check` 217/217. |

| `WJ-118` | Prepare Application's resume/cover-letter/answers editor showed raw markdown (`**`, `#`) as literal text, and required an explicit "Edit manually" → "Save version" click | ✅ Done | `lib/richtext.ts`: a small, dependency-free, bidirectional converter between the AI templates' markdown flavor (`services/ai/service.ts`: `#`/`##` headings, `**bold**`, `- ` bullets, `---` rules) and HTML — `markdownToHtml` for display/initial contentEditable content (escapes the source text before adding tags, so it can never inject markup), `htmlToMarkdown` for reading a contentEditable's live DOM back out (duck-typed against a minimal node shape so it unit-tests without a DOM library — this repo has none). `components/applications/RichTextEditor.tsx`: an uncontrolled contentEditable surface (innerHTML is only reset when `content` changes from *outside* — switching artifacts, a regenerate, a restore — never on every keystroke, or the browser's own editing would fight React and the caret would jump) with a small Bold/Italic/Heading/Bullet-list toolbar (`document.execCommand`, still broadly supported; a plain typing fallback if not). `ArtifactEditor.tsx` dropped the "Edit manually"/"Save version"/"Cancel" flow entirely — the rich-text surface is always editable, autosaving 800ms after the last keystroke (`useApplicationsStore`'s new `updateVersionContent` rewrites the *current* version's content in place rather than creating a new version — a version is a deliberate snapshot from a generation or a restore, not every keystroke; provenance flips `AI_GENERATED` → `USER_MODIFIED` the moment it's actually edited) via an inner component keyed by the version's id, so switching versions resets cleanly by remounting rather than needing an effect (avoids both an unnecessary `setState`-in-effect and, in the toolbar, a ref access during render — both flagged by this repo's React Compiler lint rules; fixed by keeping the ref-touching `execCommand` calls inside true event handlers only). The debounce is flushed on unmount so switching tabs (the parent already remounts per tab via `key={tab}`) never drops the last <800ms of typing. A small "Saving…"/"Saved" status replaces the old explicit Save button. The read-only version-compare view renders through the same `markdownToHtml`, so it's no longer raw text there either. 9 new unit tests for the markdown↔HTML conversion, including a full round-trip through a realistic resume. Verified live end to end in the browser (Playwright): typed edits render richly formatted immediately, the provenance badge flips to "User-modified" and the version count stays at 1 (no version created), the edit survives a tab-away-and-back, the Bold toolbar button works, and the actual persisted store content is confirmed to be real markdown (`**bold me**`), not HTML. `npm run check` green (238/238, full production build). |
| `WJ-119` | Download the current resume/cover letter as a real .docx from the application page | ✅ Done | `lib/zip.ts`: a minimal, dependency-free, isomorphic ZIP writer (STORED entries, so no `node:zlib`, works identically in the browser and Node) with a hand-rolled CRC-32 — round-trips through `server/resume/extractText.ts`'s existing DOCX *reader* (exported `readZipEntries`/`readZipEntry` for this), and the CRC implementation is checked against the standard IEEE 802.3 test vector (`crc32("123456789") === 0xCBF43926`). `lib/richtext.ts` gained `parseMarkdownBlocks`, the same markdown grammar `markdownToHtml` renders but as structured blocks/runs instead of HTML — one parser, so a downloaded file can never drift from what the rich-text editor shows on screen. `lib/docx.ts` turns those blocks into real Office Open XML (`word/document.xml` + `styles.xml` for heading/list styles + `numbering.xml` for real bullet-list numbering + the package/content-type boilerplate a valid .docx needs) and zips them up — entirely client-side, no server round trip, since the content is already in the browser's own state. The application detail page (`/app/applications/[id]`) shows "Download resume (.docx)" / "Download cover letter (.docx)" above "Submit on \<company\>'s site", one per artifact that actually exists (never a button for a document that wasn't generated), downloading via an in-memory `Blob` (`lib/download.ts`) with a sanitized `\<Company\>-Resume.docx` filename — no dependency, `docx` npm package or otherwise. Verification went well beyond this repo's own reader: LibreOffice's headless converter turned out to be broken in this sandbox for *any* input file including a plain .txt, so real validation used `python-docx` (an independent, spec-strict OOXML library, installed fresh for this) to open generated files — it resolved the custom heading/list styles correctly and read back every heading, bold run, italic run and bullet exactly as written. Confirmed live end to end: clicked both real download buttons in a running browser, saved the actual downloaded files, and opened them with `python-docx` — correct structure and content in both. 9 new unit tests (`zip.test.ts`, `docx.test.ts`) covering the CRC vector, a full DOCX-reader round-trip, XML escaping (a title containing `<`/`&`/`"` never produces invalid XML), and the required OOXML parts being present. `npm run check` green (251/251, full production build). |

All three adapters now read/pass the vendor's real error text. Couldn't inspect this deployment's actual Vercel env vars or logs (outside this session's connected accounts) to confirm the exact misconfiguration — most likely `WONDERJOBS_AI_MODEL` is set to a name Gemini doesn't recognize, or the key isn't a Generative Language API (AI Studio) key; the next occurrence will now say which. 4 new unit tests (`server/providers/types.test.ts`). `npm run check` 193/193. |
| `WJ-109` | Gemini's default platform model was deprecated for new users | ✅ Done | WJ-108's error-surfacing fix immediately paid off: the next real failure said exactly why — "This model models/gemini-2.5-flash is no longer available to new users. Please update your code to use models/gemini-3.6-flash." Confirmed against the live deployment (`wonder-team4/wonderjobs` on Vercel): `WONDERJOBS_AI_PROVIDER=gemini` is set, no `WONDERJOBS_AI_MODEL` override, so the code's hardcoded default was the only thing that could be stale. `platform.ts`'s `DEFAULT_MODEL.gemini` updated from `gemini-2.5-flash` to `gemini-3.6-flash` (the exact model Google's own error told us to use), and the BYOK Gemini model picker (`domain/ai/types.ts`) swapped the same deprecated option for it — `gemini-2.5-pro` (still the BYOK default) left untouched since nothing confirmed it's also deprecated and changing it without evidence would've been a guess. `npm run check` 193/193. |

Fixed real bugs: (1) `common/Button.tsx` — a `Button` with both `href` and `disabled` rendered a `next/link` `<a>` with only `aria-disabled` set; native `disabled:*` Tailwind selectors never apply to an anchor, so the button looked and behaved fully enabled and **still navigated on click** (reproduced on `/app/runs`'s "Run Wonder", meant to be disabled while a run is active). Fixed by applying the dimmed/no-pointer-events styling directly off the `disabled` prop and adding a click-guard (`preventDefault`) plus `tabIndex={-1}` on the disabled anchor; confirmed with a real click event that navigation is now blocked exactly when `aria-disabled`/the dimmed classes are present. (2) `career/CareerInsightCard.tsx` rendered a hardcoded "Your {metric} is {value} higher in product roles than last month" for *every* insight with a `metric`, fabricating a "product roles" comparison that doesn't hold for e.g. a reply-time metric (seed `ins3` has nothing to do with product roles); now bolds the metric's own value where it appears in the insight's real `body` text instead of asserting a fixed sentence. (3) `workflow/ActionApprovalList.tsx` — "Approve" on a pending external action fired immediately with no confirmation, including for the `apply` stage's `submit_application` action (`risk: "high"`) which genuinely submits a job application to an employer; added a confirmation modal gating Approve specifically for `stageKey === "apply"`, and wrapped both Approve/Decline in try/catch+toast (previously silent on failure). (4) `workflow/WorkflowControls.tsx` — the only warning that "Continue" during pending approvals records them as not-approved was a hover-only `title` attribute, invisible on touch; now shown as visible inline text; also added a "Cancelled" toast to Cancel for parity with every other action. (5) `workflow/RunErrorBanner.tsx`'s "continue"/"stop" recovery actions and (6) the mobile sticky action bar on `runs/[id]/page.tsx` (Continue/Resume/Stop) had no try/catch, unlike every sibling action — wrapped to match. (7) `calendar/CalendarSubscribe.tsx`'s clipboard copy had no error handling; a denied/unavailable `navigator.clipboard` now shows a toast instead of an unhandled rejection. `npm run check` 189/189; full Playwright suite re-run (16 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure confirmed present on the base commit too via `git stash`, 11 honestly skipped) — no regressions from these changes. |

| `WJ-081` | Google sign-in | ✅ Done | `components/auth/GoogleButton.tsx` → `signInWithOAuth({ provider: "google" })` → `/auth/callback` PKCE exchange. Until the provider is enabled in Supabase the button explains that Google sign-in isn't switched on yet. Operator steps in README. |
| `WJ-103` | A signed-in account was still shown demo mode if the browser had ever tried the demo first | ✅ Done | `getClientMode()` (`lib/mode.ts`) checked the `wj_demo` cookie *before* checking whether the browser was actually signed in, so anyone who clicked "Explore the demo" before signing up or signing in — a common flow — kept seeing seeded demo data under their real account for as long as that cookie lasted (30 days), since sign-in never cleared it either. Fixed both ends: reordered `getClientMode()` to check the real session first (matching `proxy.ts`'s own server-side priority, which already checks a verified session before the demo cookie), and `rememberUser()` (`lib/auth/browser.ts`) now clears the demo cookie outright the moment a real session is established, covering every sign-in path (password, magic link, OAuth callback, password reset) through the one function they all call. Reproduced and confirmed fixed against a real Supabase account in a real browser (entered demo, then signed in without ever visiting "Exit demo" — `wj_demo` cookie gone, "Demo mode" label gone, landed in the real account). 7 unit tests (`lib/mode.test.ts`), including a named regression test for the exact priority bug. `npm run check` 189/189. |

### Platform

| ID | Story | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WJ-090` | PWA installability | ✅ Done | `app/manifest.ts` (id, name, `start_url: "/app"`, `display: "standalone"`, shortcuts to Run/Jobs/Applications); icons generated with `next/og`'s `ImageResponse` — `app/icon.tsx` (favicon) and `app/apple-icon.tsx` (iOS) via Next's file convention, plus explicit `app/icon-192.png`, `app/icon-512.png` and `app/icon-512-maskable.png` route handlers so the manifest can reference fixed URLs. `lib/pwa.ts` (`useInstallPrompt`) captures `beforeinstallprompt` and exposes it as "Install app" in the avatar menu — Chromium only; iOS/Firefox have no such API, so the item simply doesn't render there. `public/sw.js` registered in production only (`components/pwa/RegisterServiceWorker.tsx`): deliberately does not cache any page or API response (this app is local-first and real-time already — `store/remoteStorage.ts` — so a caching service worker would risk serving stale job/run/application data), it only serves a small static offline page when a navigation's `fetch` fails. |
| `WJ-096` | Push notification delivery | ✅ Done | Web Push end to end, with no dependency: `server/push/webPush.ts` implements RFC 8291 (ECDH P-256 → HKDF-SHA256 → AES-128-GCM, `aes128gcm` framing) and RFC 8292 (ES256 VAPID JWT, DER→JOSE signature conversion) on `node:crypto`, and the tests **reproduce RFC 8291's own published test vector byte for byte** — a round-trip against our own code would have passed just as happily with the whole chain wrong. Subscriptions live in `wonderjobs.push_subscriptions` (migration `0005`), one row per browser; a 404/410 from a push service means the browser dropped the subscription, so the row is deleted rather than retried forever. `POST/GET/DELETE /api/push/subscribe` (session required, rate-limited, tenant-scoped delete so no account can unsubscribe another's browser); the POST sends a real notification straight away so "it's on" is something the candidate sees. `components/pwa/PushNotifications.tsx` on the Profile page never asks for permission on load — an uninvited prompt is how a site gets blocked permanently, and a blocked browser can't be un-blocked from the page — and the whole card is hidden on deployments with no keys. `public/sw.js` gained `push` and `notificationclick` handlers, the latter reusing an open tab instead of opening a window per notification. Wired into the scheduled-run cron: the in-app notification is saved first and is the record; the push is sent last and can never cost a run its results. Operator setup is `npm run push:keys` plus three environment variables. 17 unit tests. |

### Career DNA

| ID | Story | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WJ-095` | Import from resume | ✅ Done | `POST /api/career/import-resume` (session required, rate-limited per tenant, 5 MB cap) takes a PDF, DOCX, plain text or a pasted body and returns a **draft**, never a write: `components/career/ResumeImport.tsx` shows every suggested field with the words it came from, the candidate ticks what to keep, and only then is it applied to the Career DNA form (still unsaved). Offered on `/app/career-dna` and inside onboarding step 2. The file is read in memory and discarded — nothing is stored. Extraction is dependency-free (`server/resume/extractText.ts`): a DOCX is a ZIP read through its central directory and inflated with `node:zlib`; a text PDF is its Flate streams' `Tj`/`TJ` operators, with escapes, octal codes and hex strings decoded and undecodable streams skipped rather than failing the file. A scanned PDF has no text at all, so `looksReadable()` gates the result and the route answers 422 with "paste it instead" rather than returning an empty profile. Parsing (`server/resume/parseResume.ts`) reuses the **same** `SKILL_LEXICON`, `extractSkills` and `inferSeniority` the product uses to read job postings — that shared vocabulary is what makes a skill found in a resume actually match a skill found in a posting. Skill strength follows how often a skill runs through the document; seniority reads only lines that look like held titles ("Reported to the director." is not a directorship); years prefers a stated "N years of experience" over the earliest dated role. Career goal, salary and work modes are deliberately never guessed. 30 unit tests, including PDFs and DOCXs built byte by byte in the tests themselves and the route's multipart, JSON, 415/422/400/401 paths. |
| `WJ-112` | Resume import rejected a normal, text-based PDF as "probably a scan" | ✅ Done | Reported with a real PDF and a screenshot proving it wasn't a scan. Root-caused two independent, pre-existing bugs in `server/resume/extractText.ts`'s hand-rolled PDF reader (no parsing dependency, by design): (1) the stream-scanner's `re.lastIndex = end` pointed at the *start* of `"endstream"`, not past it — since `"endstream"` itself contains the substring `"stream"`, the very next regex search re-matched inside it as a bogus new stream, corrupting detection of every stream after the first. Any PDF with more than one stream object — which is virtually all of them, since an embedded font and (when present) its `/ToUnicode` CMap are each their own stream — silently lost every stream after the first content stream. (2) No `/ToUnicode` CMap support at all: most real PDFs (Word, Google Docs, LaTeX, "Print to PDF") embed a subsetted font that gives each glyph an arbitrary internal code, recorded as the real character only in that font's own ToUnicode stream; without reading it, glyph codes decoded to unprintable control characters or the wrong letters, correctly failing `looksReadable` — a totally normal PDF came back indistinguishable from an actual scan. Fixed both at the root: the scanner now advances past `"endstream"` fully, and a `CMap` is built from every ToUnicode stream in the file (ToUnicode markers themselves used to identify and skip those streams as non-content) and threaded through both string forms a content stream can hold, tried first for 2-byte glyph codes and falling through to the prior heuristic when nothing resolves — safe for every existing plain-ASCII PDF, since an empty map changes nothing. A third bug surfaced while verifying against a real Chromium-rendered PDF: the embedded font *program* stream and any image stream are pure binary, not drawing operators, but their bytes could coincidentally match the Tj/TJ token pattern and inject garbage that diluted otherwise-perfectly-extracted prose below the readability threshold; both are now skipped up front (a font program's dict always carries `/Length1` per the PDF spec; an image's carries `/Subtype /Image` — neither a content nor a CMap stream ever does). Verified against two independently Chromium-generated PDFs (`page.pdf()`, real subsetted fonts, no synthetic fixtures involved) end to end through the actual `/app/career-dna` import UI in a real browser: both now read as `readable: true` with clean text, and `parseResume` correctly filled years of experience, skills, industries and location from the second. A residual, lower-severity cosmetic issue remains and is knowingly out of scope here: the content-stream reader treats every text-positioning operator as a line break, so a heading or word occasionally splits across lines when a real PDF renderer emits small positioning nudges mid-run (observed on "José García-Núñez" and "VP of Engineering" in the second test PDF) — it doesn't block readability or field extraction, both worked correctly despite it. 7 new unit tests, including one that pins the `endstream`-substring bug directly and one for the font-program/image pollution. `npm run check` 212/212. |
| `WJ-113` | Same "not a scan" error, on the user's own real CV — the "cosmetic" issue from WJ-112 was the actual bug | ✅ Done | The user supplied the actual failing file. It reproduced `readable: false` in isolation, output one character per line (`extractPdfText` returned "K\nu\nn\na\nl\n..."), which is exactly what WJ-112 flagged as a minor, out-of-scope cosmetic quirk — it wasn't minor, it was the whole bug for this common PDF-generation style. This résumé (an ATS-builder export) draws every *word* — the space between two words included — as its own `BT…ET` text object for exact kerning, and marks a real new line only by re-issuing the page's `cm` coordinate transform; it never uses a vertical `Td` at all. The reader's rule of "every `Td`/`TD`/`T*`/`ET` is a line break" is correct for some generators (a browser's own PDF export puts one whole line per `BT…ET`, confirmed by inspecting a real Chromium-generated PDF's content stream — 10 `BT` blocks for 10 lines) and catastrophically wrong for this one. Neither convention can be detected from the operator alone without tracking the real coordinate-transform stack, which this reader deliberately doesn't do (no parsing dependency, by design). Fixed with a heuristic that works for both real styles without that tracking: `T*` (the one operator the spec defines as an unconditional new line) and a matched `cm` invocation are treated as a hard line break — a `cm` is never observed mid-word, only at a real visual line/paragraph boundary; a new `BT` gets a plain space instead of a break, so a word-per-object generator doesn't run every word together; bare `Td`/`TD`/`ET` are no longer treated as line breaks at all. Two smaller bugs found alongside it: a synthetic space inserted before each `BT` combined with this generator's own drawn space-glyph to double every inter-word space — `tidy()` now collapses runs of 2+ literal spaces (safe and correct for any source); and `tidy()`'s space-stripping step had always been silently inert — its regex literal was a stray NUL byte (`/\0/g`) instead of a real space, invisibly typed in wrong at some point before this session and never once matching real text — removed as dead code rather than "fixed" into a working space-stripper, which would have deleted every space between every word in every PDF. Verified against the user's actual CV end to end through the real `/app/career-dna` import UI: `readable: true`, and the draft correctly filled name, headline, years of experience (9, from "earliest role starts 2017"), current level (Director), 14 matched skills and industries — also re-verified both earlier Chromium-generated test PDFs still extract cleanly, headings intact, no regressions. 3 new unit tests reproducing the word-per-`BT`/line-per-`cm` pattern directly. `npm run check` 215/215. |

### Testing

| ID | Story | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WJ-102` | Playwright E2E infrastructure + `auth.spec.ts` and `golden-journeys.spec.ts`, actually executed | 🟡 In progress | `apps/web/playwright.config.ts` + `apps/web/e2e/` stood up (`@playwright/test`, 5-project browser matrix, real Supabase backend — never mocked) and `auth.spec.ts` (18 tests) actually run against chromium: 13 passed, 5 honestly skipped, 0 failed, stable across repeated runs. Test accounts are created/deleted per test via the Supabase Admin API (`email_confirm: true`, never sends mail). Getting a real browser (not just CLI tools) through this sandbox's TLS-intercepting proxy needed `use.proxy` plus a static `--ignore-certificate-errors` launch flag (the per-connection `ignoreHTTPSErrors` context option wasn't enough — the proxy mints a fresh leaf cert per connection, which defeats Chromium's per-cert exception cache and produces `net::ERR_TOO_MANY_RETRIES`), both gated on `HTTPS_PROXY` so they no-op elsewhere. **Found and fixed a real product defect along the way:** `GET /demo` (`app/demo/route.ts`) unconditionally set the `wj_demo` cookie, which `proxy.ts` treats as authorization to skip the sign-in requirement on `/app`/`/onboarding`; Next.js's automatic `<Link>` prefetching (the marketing page's "Explore the demo" buttons use `Button`, which renders `next/link`) sends this exact request — tagged `next-router-prefetch: 1` — the moment the link scrolls into view, well before any click, silently flipping any landing-page visitor into demo mode. Surfaced because `AUTH-016` (protected routes reject access again after sign-out) genuinely failed: signing out lands on `/`, which renders those buttons, and the very next `/app` request wasn't redirected to sign-in. Fixed by skipping the cookie set when that header is present. Also fixed two test-authoring bugs found on first real execution: a `getByLabel("Password")` strict-mode violation (matched both the password field and the "Show password" toggle; needed `{ exact: true }`), and `AUTH-017`'s original draft using an unnamespaced localStorage key that never exercised the real per-tenant isolation logic (`` `${userId}:${name}` ``, `lib/mode.ts`) — rewritten to use the real key shape, which then correctly surfaced that `signOutEverywhere` clears the *signing-out account's own* local keys too (by design: local state is a cache, the server document is the source of truth on next sign-in), so `AUTH-007` was rewritten to assert the real, server-synced signal (onboarding-completion survives a sign-out/sign-in round trip for the same account) rather than a fabricated local marker. `AUTH-003` (real sign-up through the UI) is an honest, documented skip: this Supabase project has "Confirm email" on, and every domain tried either fails validation outright (`example.com`) or gets far enough to attempt a real send (confirmed via GoTrue's own rate limiter) — no domain exists that's both valid and guaranteed mail-free, so exercising it would violate the "never send real external email" rule. Firefox/WebKit/Mobile Safari confirmed BLOCKED by an actual launch attempt (no binaries in this sandbox), not assumed. `golden-journeys.spec.ts` (7 tests, entirely in demo mode — no real account needed, since demo mode auto-seeds a full job catalog, applications and Career DNA synchronously on boot and never gates behind onboarding) covers demo entry via a real click (not a prefetch, closing the loop on the bug above), the jobs list and a job's detail/match-explanation/save toggle, the "not for me" flow with a reason and undo, the applications dashboard's per-status routing (a submitted application opens its real timeline; a saved/preparing one instead opens the Prepare Application flow — confirmed both paths), and starting a Wonder run landing on that run's own timeline page. 7/7 passed, stable across a repeated run (14/14 on `--repeat-each=2`). Found two test-authoring bugs on first execution (both in the new spec's own assertions, not the product): a strict-mode selector collision between the sidebar's "Applications" link and the page's own back link, and a `waitForURL` target pattern that also matched the starting `/app/runs/new` URL itself (`"new"` satisfies `[^/]+` just like a real run id), so it resolved before the real navigation happened — fixed by excluding `"new"` explicitly. Full results, defects and fixes in `apps/web/docs/TEST_EXECUTION_REPORT.md`. **Remaining:** automation (scheduled runs, policy settings), Career DNA editing, BYOK/AI provider settings and PWA/push flows have no E2E coverage; golden journeys cover demo mode only, not a real signed-in account with genuine (non-seeded) data. |
